properties.name: MEASURED at the v0.78.0 cut, 2026-10-03: a v0.77.0 binary opens a design that stores Verification.last_reconciled_outcome = blocked with no refusal, re-stamps it 0.77.0, and then writes an export it cannot import
properties.source: the v0.77.0 release asset reflow2-mcp-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (sha256 0e86d155…, matching the release's checksums.txt) and the 0.78.0 debug build of branch cut-v0.78.0
properties.statement: OBSERVED: in a scratch store, 0.78.0 wrote a Verification and reconcile_verification recorded outcome `blocked`; the store's stamp (graph.meta.json) read 0.78.0, with `blocked` in Verification.last_reconciled_outcome. The v0.77.0 release binary then ran `--call graph_report` and `--call get_node` on it: exit 0, no refusal, and the value was read back as "blocked". Afterwards the stamp read 0.77.0 and its enum record no longer listed `blocked`. `--export` by 0.77.0 succeeded, and `--import` of that export by 0.77.0 was refused, all or nothing ("invalid enum value 'blocked', expected one of [passed, failed, skipped]"); 0.78.0 imported it. EXPECTED: the guard cap:stamp and the v0.59.0 and v0.65.0 upgrade notes describe, a refusal naming the value and both versions, because the store HOLDS the value. WHERE IT BREAKS (read in code, and consistent with every measurement): in 0.77.0 only provenance::check_and_stamp writes the stamp, so it ran with the unknown value in hand; its population probe (the enum_population closure in Graph::open_rocksdb_with_provenance) asks StorageEngine::scan_nodes_by_property, whose own doc says it scans the property index CF_NODE_IDX only. last_reconciled_outcome is not `indexed: true`, so the probe answers "not stored" and the open proceeds and re-stamps. The two earlier enum moves (Decision.status `deferred`, ChangeEvent.change_type `decision_settled`) are both indexed, which is why their guard held. ver:a-vocabulary-change-is-never-silent passes because it supplies the population through a closure, for Decision.status only, so the engine probe is never exercised on a non-indexed property. THE CLASS: 4 of the 69 enum vocabularies the stamp records are not indexed: Constraint.direction, Fragment.note_kind, Project.mode, Verification.last_reconciled_outcome. A new value on any of them is invisible to an older binary's guard. ALSO MEASURED: the stamp records node enum vocabularies only; the 30 enum properties declared on edge types are not in it. NOT ESTABLISHED: a direct engine-level measurement of the index scan on that property (the cause is read from code, not instrumented), and whether leaving edge enums out of the stamp was deliberate (dec:the-stamp-records-enum-values-and-nothing-finer). The fix cannot reach a v0.77.0 binary, which has already shipped; v0.78.0's upgrade note says what that binary does instead.
